# The RT64 shaders the web page builds: one shader description a line, other mode L and H, color combiner L and H,
# flags, in hex. RT64 specializes each one's WGSL when the page is built and builds them with the game waiting: those
# above the first "section" line before the game starts, and a section when the game first draws with 4 of its shaders,
# so that nothing draws with the ubershader, which integrated graphics can't afford (N64Recomp-browser's
# docs/porting.md, Prebuilt shader lists).
#
# Recorded by code, not by playing: bash tools/record_shaders.sh (its header says how) runs N64Recomp-browser's
# tools/record_shaders.mjs with tools/shader_plan.json, which loads the page fresh for each section. Section 0 is the
# launcher, the logos, the opening and the title as they play by themselves and with Start (Enter), and Mushroom Village
# on a new save. RulesBoard is A (Space) through Toad's messages and the warp pipe into the board Toad teaches the rules
# on, then 90 s of A with four computer players on it. Then a section for each board, DKsJungleAdventure to EternalStar,
# a minute of A on each; one for each minigame, MemoryMatch to BumperBallMaze3 (the decomp's names, Minigame2A for 0x2A,
# a number after the name for Slot Car Derby's and Bumper Ball Maze's other courses), each opened as a board opens it,
# by its instructions screen with the players on its sides, then Start, and played by the computer players to its end,
# and Chance Time, a board's event, gone to directly; and one for each of the village's places, MinigameHouse to
# OptionsHouse, 30 s of A in each, and MinigameIsland, its start screen (0x78) and its introduction, A until the island
# (0x71) or 150 s, then 30 s more (on the survey's save it leaves for the rules' board, not the island, so the island's
# own shaders aren't in it). The survey (patches/survey.c, tools/survey.js) sends the hub's trips to the rules' board to
# each board, minigame's instructions or Chance Time, and the warp pipe to each place, as tools/shader_plan.json says.
